Note TeX Accessor API Reference¶

Back to Note API Reference

Note::tex() is the TeX/LaTeX-source operation boundary for Note. It keeps generic text mechanics on Note while collecting operations whose meaning depends on TeX syntax: comments, preamble, math delimiters, commands, environments, macros, and the semantic structures (theorems, citations, labels, sections, …) that TeX/LaTeX source encodes.

The accessor is zero-overhead plumbing: obtaining it performs no transform and does not enlarge Note. Every terminal method is still batched over all cells and returns either a shape-preserving Note or a closed TokenBatch containing Text tokens and Int64 offsets.

TokenBatch has its own method reference. Use it to learn the flattened token Note, cumulative offsets, defined/empty state, and borrowed-reference lifetime shared by every ragged extraction result.

Canonical Surface¶

The accessor deliberately omits duplicate spellings. Earlier flat-Note tex_* methods that were pure aliases — 15 tex_replace_<greek-letter>() convenience wrappers around cmd_sub(name, repl) with a literal command name baked in, 12 tex_remove_env_<name>() wrappers around strip_env(name), 12 tex_extract_env_<name>() wrappers plus tex_arrays() and 6 semantic-block wrappers (tex_theorems(), tex_lemmas(), …) all around what is now env(name) — were deleted rather than carried over. env(name) also gained real capability in the move: it now always returns the full closed TokenBatch (tokens plus row offsets), where the old flat Note::tex_extract_environment(name) silently discarded the offsets and returned only the flat token Note.

collapse_whitespace() is intentionally absent from this accessor. Its former implementation was exactly the root Note::collapse_whitespace operation, with no TeX-specific rule, so the duplicate spelling was removed.

Writing the standardize_* family surfaced a genuine bug, since fixed at the source rather than documented as a workaround: seven internal TeX-generation helpers (backing vector_norm, matrix_norm, int_norm, prime_norm, simplify_fractions, simplify_roots, and the mode >= 1 \sqrt(...) path of to_latex, inserted a doubled backslash into their output — \\vec{v} instead of \vec{v} — which real LaTeX reads as a forced linebreak followed by literal text, not the intended command. Every affected method now emits the single, TeX-correct backslash; the fix carries no behavioral change beyond removing the extra character.

Coverage¶

Every method on the accessor now has a full, compiled-and-verified page — all ninety-seven:

  • add_math_delimiters: make every non-empty cell one complete math fragment while preserving an existing outer delimiter style.

  • align_blocks: extract complete align and align* environments in document order with per-cell offsets.

  • args: select balanced required arguments from one exact control word while preserving lane ownership.

  • balance_braces / balance_math_delims: repair lexical group and math-delimiter structure without pretending to validate TeX.

  • bibliography_keys: extract individual citation and bibitem identifiers as a closed ragged result.

  • canonicalize_macros / collapse_macros: normalize built-in control words or compact source by removing local declarations.

  • captions / citations: extract semantic command arguments while retaining per-cell ownership.

  • cmd_sub: replace one exact control word with literal caller-provided text without consuming attached groups.

  • command_names: inventory lexical TeX control words without confusing control symbols for names.

  • commands: extract either bare control-word lexemes or complete calls with balanced attached argument groups.

  • deaccent: unwrap exact TeX accent commands and fold accented UTF-8 Latin characters without damaging ordinary commands.

  • frac_slash / sqrt_pow: translate balanced fraction and root constructs into explicit arithmetic text.

  • graphics_tags: retain graphic paths as visible tags without filesystem access or option interpretation.

  • pm_signs: render paired-sign control words without corrupting longer command names.

  • dedup_blank_lines: cap vertical whitespace while preserving the source line-ending convention.

  • display_math: extract complete display fragments while retaining their original delimiters and cell ownership.

  • env_names / envs: inventory environment openers or extract complete begin/end regions.

  • env: extract one exact environment kind with nested same-name regions balanced as one token.

  • figures: extract complete ordinary and starred figure regions in source order, including balanced same-name nesting.

  • fix_linebreaks: normalize physical line endings, remove trailing horizontal whitespace, and cap blank-line runs.

  • footnotes: extract balanced footnote bodies while distinguishing optional marks from authored content.

  • headings: build a lane-aware outline through an explicit structural depth rather than an accidental result-count limit.

  • includes: inventory input, include, and graphics targets without filesystem access or path rewriting.

  • input_tags: retain external-input targets as visible tags without reading the filesystem.

  • line_norm: canonicalize CRLF and CR line endings to LF without otherwise reformatting source.

  • inline_math / math_blocks / math_only: extract inline regions, retain one all-form region stream, or project each cell onto joined formula bodies.

  • labels: extract balanced cross-reference anchor bodies while rejecting escaped, longer, and incomplete command forms.

  • macro_defs / macro_use: inventory complete local declarations or each cell’s first-seen control-word vocabulary.

  • macro_subs: substitute cell-local simple macros with an explicit, deterministic recursion bound.

  • packages: extract individual package names from complete package declarations while retaining per-cell ownership.

  • refs: extract balanced targets from the supported cross-reference command families.

  • render: project common TeX notation and symbols into compact readable Unicode with bounded local-macro expansion.

  • sections: extract exact top-level section titles into a closed ragged result with per-cell offsets.

  • set_macro: install one canonical cell-local definition while replacing complete prior declarations of the same name.

  • simplify_fractions / simplify_roots: canonicalize balanced fraction or root calls while retaining TeX source.

  • strip_bib / strip_cites: remove complete bibliography machinery or citation calls through balanced lexical scans.

  • strip_cmds: remove control words and every immediately attached balanced argument group.

  • strip_color: discard color styling while retaining visible wrapper content.

  • strip_comments: remove unescaped comments while preserving LF, CRLF, and CR physical line endings.

  • strip_delims: remove the six lexical math delimiter spellings while preserving escaped dollar signs and cell shape.

  • strip_env: remove one validated environment kind with same-name nesting balanced.

  • strip_envs: remove every complete, properly nested environment region while preserving malformed source.

  • strip_figs / strip_graphics: remove figure-family regions alone, or remove those regions together with direct graphic calls.

  • strip_fmt / strip_fonts: retain visible bodies while removing wrapper formatting, optionally including font declarations.

  • strip_labels: remove complete label anchors without consuming escaped, longer, or malformed command text.

  • strip_links: remove destinations while retaining the visible labels of href and hyperref calls.

  • strip_lr: remove exact automatic delimiter-size modifiers without damaging longer commands such as leftarrow.

  • strip_macro: remove complete declarations of one validated macro name while retaining its use sites and other definitions.

  • strip_metadata: remove balanced title-page declarations and the bare title-rendering command.

  • strip_pkgs: remove balanced package and document-class declarations while preserving malformed source.

  • strip_preamble: isolate the body between complete exact document boundaries, preserving incomplete source.

  • strip_refs: remove complete calls from the supported cross-reference families through an exact balanced scan.

  • strip_size: remove exact big-family sizing commands while retaining delimiters and their contents.

  • strip_space: remove exact explicit-spacing controls while preserving malformed or escaped syntax.

  • strip_tables: remove complete balanced table structures without changing the receiver’s shape.

  • escape / to_text: protect literal text for TeX source or reduce authored TeX to readable text.

  • vector_norm / matrix_norm: canonicalize vector notation and bracketed matrix environments to one spelling each.

  • int_norm / sum_norm / limit_norm: collapse multi-integral and summation command spellings, and strip the \limits/\nolimits position modifier.

  • sub_norm / sup_norm / prime_norm: brace every bare _/^ script and rewrite trailing ' marks as an explicit \prime superscript.

  • dots_norm: collapse ellipsis command spellings to \dots.

  • math_funcs / greek: classify recognized function and lowercase Greek control words inside complete math regions.

  • ids / nums / ops / symbols: extract complementary lexical views of authored mathematics.

  • subsections / subsubsections: extract heading titles one and two levels below sections.

  • tables / tabular_blocks: extract complete floating-table and row/column environments, starred forms included.

  • text_only: the exact prose-preserving mirror of math_only.

  • to_html / to_markdown: convert a recognized TeX subset to HTML or Markdown markup; to_markdown additionally takes a case-folding mode that to_html has no counterpart for.

  • to_latex: build TeX source up from plain text, the inverse direction from to_text.

  • todos / warnings: extract authoring notes or embedded compiler diagnostics.

  • unescape: the exact inverse of escape.

  • wrap_inline_math / wrap_display_math: add math delimiters explicitly, with different existing-delimiter handling between the two.
